headline: Ohio State vs Michigan recap: Buckeyes win 45-0 in The Game

paragraphs.text: Well, that was more like it.

Ohio State beat Michigan 45-0 on Saturday at Ohio Stadium, closing the regular season the way the rivalry demands — with a record, a breakout running back, and a brawl for good measure. It was the largest margin of victory in the history of The Game, and the first time the Buckeyes have shut out Michigan since 1962.

The Buckeyes are 8-4 now, 6-3 in the Big Ten, and they finish the regular season on the highest of notes. Michigan falls to 6-6, 3-6 in the conference. There was no Big Ten title or College Football Playoff berth on the line in this one. There was only The Game, and Ohio State took it in front of 105,708 fans.
Ohio State vs Michigan: How the Buckeyes won it

Ohio State wasted no time. The Buckeyes took the opening kickoff, and after a Michigan personal foul gave them the ball at their own 40, they marched 60 yards in six plays. Luke Fahey hit three big passes on the drive, found Bo Jackson on an 18-yard pass to the Michigan one, and Jackson punched it in from a yard out with 11:32 left in the first quarter. Ohio State 7, Michigan 0.

The second quarter belonged to Jeremiah Smith. After Michigan missed a 30-yard field goal, Ohio State put together a 13-play, 80-yard drive that took 6:48 off the clock, and Fahey found Smith for a five-yard touchdown with 13:29 left in the half. It was Smith's first catch of the game, his 18th receiving touchdown of the season — breaking Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record of 17, set in 1995 — and he struck the Heisman pose in the end zone. It was also the first time since 1995 that Ohio State scored on its first two drives of The Game. Ohio State 14, Michigan 0.

Jackson struck again with 5:22 left in the half, taking a handoff on the first play of the drive and running 29 yards through a facemask penalty for his second touchdown of the day. Ohio State 21, Michigan 0, and that was the halftime score.

The second half was more of the same. Connor Hawkins' 32-yard field goal with 8:25 left in the third quarter, capping a nearly six-minute drive, made it 24-0. Michigan's best drive of the day ended on downs when Qua Russaw sacked Bryce Underwood on fourth-and-8 with 4:14 left in the quarter. Then Jackson completed his hat trick with an eight-yard touchdown run with 1:13 left in the third, finishing an eight-play, 72-yard drive. Ohio State 31, Michigan 0 after three quarters.

Smith added two more in the fourth. He caught a two-yard touchdown with 9:00 left — an 11-play, 49-yard drive — to tie Desmond Howard's Big Ten single-season record of 19. Ohio State 38, Michigan 0. Michigan's one would-be score, a 70-yard fumble return by Aisea Moa, was wiped out on review. Then, after an offensive pass interference call erased one touchdown catch, Smith hauled in a pass on fourth-and-13 with 1:45 left for his third touchdown of the day and his 20th of the season, breaking Howard's record outright. Ohio State 45, Michigan 0, and that was the final.
Bo Jackson and Jeremiah Smith lead Ohio State vs Michigan
If there is a one-line version of this game, it is Jackson and Smith.

Jackson was the workhorse with Ja'Kobi Jackson out, and he ran like it all afternoon: 24 carries for 170 yards and three touchdowns, plus three catches for 69 yards — 239 yards from scrimmage in the game of his career. He scored the first touchdown of the game and the one that made it a three-score game, and he did it running through contact both times. Jackson is now the second Buckeye ever to rush for 1,000 yards as a freshman and a sophomore, joining J.K. Dobbins.

Smith did not need many touches to make history. His first catch of the game was the record-breaker, and he finished with eight catches for 90 yards and three touchdowns. That gave him 94 catches and 1,572 yards for the season, with 20 touchdowns — breaking Glenn's Ohio State record and Howard's Big Ten record. He finished one catch short of Jaxon Smith-Njigba's single-season record of 95, and 34 yards short of Smith-Njigba's 1,606.

Fahey, the true freshman starting with Julian Sayin out for the season with a fractured elbow, was calm from the start and finished 18 of 36 for 253 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Along the way, he broke Terrelle Pryor's record for passing yards in a season by a true freshman.
Ohio State defense shuts down Michigan
The defense that had given up 30-plus points in three of its last four games held Michigan to 150 total yards and kept the Wolverines off the scoreboard.

Bryce Underwood, cleared to start after being listed as questionable all week with a lower-body injury, never got comfortable. He finished 9 of 17 for 86 yards with an interception, and the Buckeyes sacked him three times, two of them by Khary Wilder. Jaylen McClain had the interception. Michigan managed seven first downs all day, and its only real scoring chance was the missed 30-yard field goal on its opening drive.

Ohio State outgained Michigan 484-150, held the ball for 35:21, and went 6-for-6 in the red zone. It was the Buckeyes' tenth shutout of Michigan all time, and the first shutout in the rivalry since Michigan beat Ohio State 28-0 in 1993.
What Ohio State's win over Michigan means
First, the bowl picture. The Buckeyes will learn their bowl destination on Dec. 6, with the Citrus Bowl, ReliaQuest Bowl and Music City Bowl among the possibilities.

Second, Ryan Day. He came into the day 2-4 against Michigan, with both wins coming in Ann Arbor and no win over the Wolverines in Columbus. Now he has his first home win in the rivalry, Ohio State's first win over Michigan in the Shoe since 2018, and the Buckeyes' first back-to-back wins over Michigan since the eight-game winning streak that ended in 2019. Day is now 3-4 in The Game.

Third, Smith. He got the biggest record on his first catch of the afternoon, then broke the Big Ten record for good measure. He finished one catch and 34 yards short of Smith-Njigba's single-season records — marks that will stand unless he plays in the bowl game.
